newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct in speculative trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.02 percent to close at 1.0304 per dollar in speculative trade on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Some banks had expected that foreign investors who acquired a majority stake in Rio de Janeiro power utility Cerj on Wednesday would pay for the shares today, and the banks sold dollars in advance.

But when it became clear that the dollars from Cerj's privatization would not be injected into the market today, banks decided to cover their short positions by buying dollars, leading the real to hit 1.0312, a drop of 0.06 percent from Wednesday's close.
The market was calmer in the afternoon and the local currency recovered.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating-rate market, the real ended flat at 1.0362 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.27 percent to close at 1.095 per dollar.
